features.label: Parity
features.doc: How many births she has had before. First labours are longer and behave differently from later ones.

features.label: FHR spread, last 30 min
features.doc: How wide the spread of heart rates has been over the last 30 minutes. A wide spread usually means the rate is swinging, most often from repeated decelerations. Not a FIGO concept, but the strongest single feature in this dataset.

features.label: Total time above 160 bpm
features.doc: Total minutes spent tachycardic since the recording began. Sustained tachycardia can be an early compensation sign.

features.label: Maternal age
features.doc: The mother's age at delivery. A background risk factor, not a property of this trace, and constant for the whole labour.

features.label: Most common FHR so far
features.doc: The single heart rate this fetus has spent more of labour at than any other -- its settled resting rate across the whole recording.

features.label: Minutes of tachysystole so far
features.doc: How much of this labour has been spent above 5 contractions per 10 minutes, counted minute by minute since the recording began. The dose rather than the state: a uterus can be contracting normally right now and have spent the previous hour over the line, and the reserve spent there does not come back. Nearly independent of how long the recording has run (r = 0.19 with elapsed minutes), so it is not a relabelled clock.

features.label: Total acceleration time so far
features.doc: Total seconds spent in accelerations since the recording began, on the same definition -- post-deceleration overshoot does not count. Being cumulative it only ever rises, so it carries how long the labour has run as well as how much of it was reassuring.

features.label: Contraction rate over the whole labour
features.doc: Average contraction rate since the recording began.

features.label: Usable FHR since the start
features.doc: The share of the whole recording so far that carried a usable FHR signal. The two 30-minute quality features say whether the trace is readable now; this says whether it ever was, which is a different question about a record whose sensor has been on and off all labour.

features.label: Gravidity
features.doc: How many times this woman has been pregnant, this one included.

features.label: Contractions per 10 min, last 30 min
features.doc: Current contraction rate. More than 5 per 10 minutes is tachysystole, which shortens the recovery time between contractions.

features.label: Lowest FHR so far
features.doc: The lowest heart rate reached at any point since the recording began.

features.label: Accelerations per 10 min, last 30 min
features.doc: How often the heart rate is rising above baseline right now, on the same overshoot-excluding definition as the 60-minute version. Half the lookback, so it answers whether the fetus is still reacting rather than whether it reacted this hour -- at the cost of being read off a window that often contains no acceleration at all.

features.label: Signal quality, last 30 min
features.doc: The share of the last 30 minutes with usable FHR. Carried as a feature rather than used to exclude records, so poor recording shows up as an explicit contribution instead of silently biasing the score.

features.label: Variable decelerations per 10 min, last 30 min
features.doc: Abrupt drops that vary in shape and timing from one contraction to the next, typically cord compression. Common and usually tolerated, but they are what turns concerning when they deepen or stop recovering.

features.label: Time below 110 bpm, last 60 min
features.doc: The share of the last hour spent below 110 bpm, the bottom of the normal band.

features.label: Meconium-stained liquor
features.doc: Meconium seen in the liquor (1 yes, 0 no). Observed during labour, not from the trace, and a long-standing marker of fetal compromise.

features.label: Contractions followed by a deceleration, last 30 min
features.doc: The share of contractions the fetus did not absorb without dipping. A rate of decelerations means little without knowing how many contractions there were to cause them -- three in an hour of frequent contractions is a different trace from three in an hour of six.

features.label: Short-term variability, last 30 min
features.doc: Average change between consecutive 3.75-second epochs (the Dawes-Redman measure). Falls before most other signs of distress.

features.label: Baseline, last 30 min
features.doc: The resting heart rate over the last 30 minutes, with accelerations and decelerations excluded. FIGO normal is 110-160.

features.label: Variability, last 30 min
features.doc: How much the heart rate wobbles around its own baseline, measured only between events so decelerations cannot inflate it. FIGO calls under 5 reduced and over 25 marked.

features.label: Late decelerations per 10 min, last 30 min
features.doc: Decelerations that begin after the contraction has peaked and recover after it ends. This is the pattern that points at the placenta rather than the cord or the head, and FIGO treats it as the concerning one even when it is shallow.

features.label: Low-variability minutes per 10 min, last 60 min
features.doc: How much of the last hour had variability under 5 bpm. A sustained run of flat trace is more concerning than a brief dip.

features.label: Minutes since second stage began
features.doc: How long the woman has been pushing: zero through the first stage, then rising minute by minute. Read the value, not the onset -- CTU-CHB places the onset at exactly 60.0 min in 97% of records, so this is really "minutes of trace past the 60-minute mark". It tracks the header's true second-stage duration at r = 0.99 and is strongly graded against outcome (15% acidaemic under 5 min, 48% over 20), which is why it is carried despite the convention.

features.label: TOCO quality, last 30 min
features.doc: The share of the last 30 minutes with a usable contraction trace. Every uterine-activity feature is a rate measured off this channel, so without it a record whose TOCO was unreadable is indistinguishable from one whose uterus was genuinely quiet.

features.label: Accelerations per 10 min, last 60 min
features.doc: Accelerations reflect an intact autonomic response and are reassuring. Rises that begin within 60 s of a deceleration ending are excluded: those are the recovery limb overshooting the baseline, not an acceleration, and counting them made this feature look harmful. The model may still push risk UP on a high value -- that is a suppressor effect in how contributions are split between correlated features, not a finding that accelerations are bad.

features.label: Minutes since recording started
features.doc: How long this trace has been running. Time to delivery is NOT available -- the bedside does not know when the baby will be born.

features.label: In second stage now
features.doc: Whether this minute falls after the onset of pushing. The flag the second-stage clock is counted from, carried separately because the step from first to second stage is not the same quantity as how long the second stage has run.

features.label: Maternal pyrexia
features.doc: Maternal fever in labour (1 yes, 0 no). Fever raises the fetal baseline on its own and often signals infection.
